speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an infant with recurrent stridor and wheezing; please know that any information provided here is for medical assessment only. To start, at what specific age did these symptoms first appear, and do they occur more frequently during feeding or crying?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Laryngomalacia. The combination of stridor and wheezing that worsens with crying, feeding, and neck flexion, alongside post-prandial vomiting, is classic for this condition. I would like to confirm the presence of feeding difficulties or significant failure to thrive before finalizing the plan. REQUEST TEST: Growth parameters. REQUEST TEST: Feeding assessment.
